title: Reading and Setting Scroll Positions
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of reading and setting scroll positions in a jQuery application.
Apply .scrolltop() in a small example and describe its expected result.
Verify .scrollleft() with an explicit test or browser observation.
status_note: Draft generated from the attached syllabus and official references; requires lesson-by-lesson technical review, local execution, accessibility checks, and editorial approval.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will work through reading and setting scroll positions with a focused jQuery example. The subtopics below preserve the supplied curriculum coverage and connect the API idea to a small browser interface.
content.why_it_matters: This topic is useful because it turns .scrolltop() into a repeatable implementation choice. jQuery can read dimensions, positioning, scroll offsets, and computed CSS. Prefer classes and responsive CSS for presentation state, and avoid mixing layout reads with repeated writes.

common_mistakes: Assuming a selector matched an element without checking the collection length.
Confusing jQuery collections with native DOM elements or live properties with markup attributes.
Using .html() with untrusted data or assuming client-side validation enforces server rules.
